macro_physics_principles.title: Preserve the immutable PDE contract
macro_physics_principles.implication: The equation, domain, physical parameters, conditions, metrics, budget, and seed remain immutable during algorithm design.
design_requirements: Never compensate for optimization difficulty by changing the PDE.
risks: A numerically easier altered equation is not the requested physical problem.

macro_physics_principles.title: Coupled equation and constraint consistency
macro_physics_principles.implication: Governing residuals and all available initial and boundary constraints form one coupled physical system.
design_requirements: Diagnose tradeoffs instead of dropping difficult constraints.
risks: A low residual for an under-constrained problem is not a valid solution.

macro_physics_principles.title: Initial-value causality and forward error propagation
macro_physics_principles.implication: Later-time residual reduction must not destroy consistency with the initial state, because state and approximation errors propagate forward.
risks: Late-time fitting can hide accumulated early-time error.

macro_physics_principles.title: Localized sharp-gradient structure
macro_physics_principles.implication: Solution and residual error can concentrate in narrow shock or steep-gradient regions.
design_requirements: Retain coverage away from the shock.
risks: Focusing only on the shock can degrade global accuracy.

macro_physics_principles.title: Convection–diffusion competition
macro_physics_principles.implication: Transport can move or sharpen structures faster than physical or numerical diffusion smooths them.
design_requirements: Avoid artificial smoothing of transported structures.
risks: Residual reduction can coexist with excessive numerical diffusion.

macro_physics_principles.title: Diffusive smoothing and transient consistency
macro_physics_principles.implication: Diffusion smooths spatial irregularities while the transient remains anchored by initial and boundary data.
risks: Excessive smoothing bias can erase legitimate transients.

macro_physics_principles.title: Finite wave propagation and oscillatory structure
macro_physics_principles.implication: Wave solutions carry phase and frequency information along finite-speed characteristics.
risks: Small local amplitude error can accumulate into large phase error.

macro_physics_principles.title: Initial displacement and velocity consistency
macro_physics_principles.implication: Second-order wave evolution is determined jointly by the initial displacement and initial velocity.
design_requirements: Represent and audit both initial conditions.
risks: Satisfying only displacement leaves the propagation problem incomplete.

macro_physics_principles.title: Wave-boundary reflection or periodic consistency
macro_physics_principles.implication: Boundary conditions determine whether propagating energy reflects, transmits, or wraps periodically.
design_requirements: Keep boundary treatment consistent with the stated physical topology.
risks: Incorrect boundary behavior contaminates the full space-time solution.

macro_physics_principles.title: Elliptic regularity and global boundary control
macro_physics_principles.implication: For elliptic equations, interior behavior is globally coupled to forcing and boundary data.
design_requirements: Cover the full domain and boundary.
risks: Sparse boundary coverage can bias the entire solution.

macro_physics_principles.title: Well-posedness and complete physical constraints
macro_physics_principles.implication: A low residual is meaningful only when the equation is supplied with the complete conditions needed for a well-posed solution.
design_requirements: Represent every required boundary, initial, interface, data, or auxiliary condition.
risks: An under-constrained approximation can have low residual but no unique physical meaning.

macro_physics_principles.title: Phase-accurate transport of moving structures
macro_physics_principles.implication: Advection transports structure without implying a shock; phase and location errors are primary failure modes.
risks: Do not assume shock-specific regularization without a sharp-gradient feature.

macro_physics_principles.title: Reaction–diffusion scale and rate balance
macro_physics_principles.implication: Fast reaction rates and diffusive spatial coupling create competing temporal and spatial scales.
risks: A dominant residual term can hide failure on the other physical process.

macro_physics_principles.title: Material-interface state and flux consistency
macro_physics_principles.implication: Across a coefficient or material interface, the admissible field behavior is determined jointly by the governing equation and the registered transmission or flux conditions.
design_requirements: Resolve both sides of each interface.
Do not smooth a physical material discontinuity into a different PDE.
risks: A small average residual can hide a localized flux mismatch at an interface.

macro_physics_principles.title: Spatially varying coefficient and local balance
macro_physics_principles.implication: Local propagation, diffusion, or flux scales follow the registered coefficient field rather than a single domain-wide characteristic value.
design_requirements: Resolve high-gradient coefficient regions and geometry transitions.
risks: Uniform resolution can underfit the physically hardest coefficient regime.

macro_physics_principles.title: Incompressible momentum and mass coupling
macro_physics_principles.implication: Velocity and pressure form one coupled field: momentum balance and the divergence-free constraint must hold simultaneously throughout the flow domain.
design_requirements: Retain every momentum and continuity residual component.
Preserve no-slip, inflow, outflow, and moving-wall conditions exactly as registered.
risks: Low momentum residual with nonzero divergence is not an admissible incompressible flow.

macro_physics_principles.title: Coupled-field component balance
macro_physics_principles.implication: In a multi-field PDE, each state component and equation participates in a coupled physical solution even when their numerical scales differ.
design_requirements: Prevent a large-scale field from masking a smaller coupled field.
risks: An aggregate loss can look acceptable while one physical component remains unresolved.

macro_physics_principles.title: Chaotic sensitivity and long-horizon physical fidelity
macro_physics_principles.implication: Chaotic and pattern-forming systems amplify small state and derivative errors, so long-horizon pointwise agreement is more demanding than short-time residual reduction.
design_requirements: Preserve periodicity, active modes, and coupled reaction or high-order terms.
risks: Late-time pointwise divergence may reflect accumulated phase error, while an apparently smooth trajectory may have lost the correct dynamics entirely.

macro_physics_principles.title: Helmholtz wavenumber and phase balance
macro_physics_principles.implication: The Helmholtz field balances curvature against a wavenumber-dependent reaction term, making phase and wavelength part of the physical contract.
design_requirements: Audit amplitude and phase rather than only mean error.
risks: Under-resolution can produce a smooth field with the wrong wavelength or phase.

macro_physics_principles.title: Noisy inverse observation and physics identifiability
macro_physics_principles.implication: An inferred coefficient or source is physically meaningful only when noisy observations and the governing equation constrain it sufficiently and consistently.
design_requirements: Keep observation noise distinct from PDE violation.
Audit the inferred field or parameter separately from state prediction.
risks: A low state error does not prove that the inferred physical quantity is unique or correct.

macro_physics_principles.title: Complex-geometry boundary and topology consistency
macro_physics_principles.implication: Holes, obstacles, corners, and disconnected boundary components alter admissible fluxes and field structure and are part of the physical domain, not sampling noise.
design_requirements: Maintain coverage near corners, holes, and narrow regions.
Do not fill excluded geometry with interior collocation points.
risks: Missing a small boundary component can change the global physical solution.

macro_physics_principles.title: High-dimensional measure and boundary scaling
macro_physics_principles.implication: Interior volume, boundary measure, and low-discrepancy coverage scale differently as dimension grows, so low-dimensional point-count intuition is unreliable.
design_requirements: Audit interior and boundary coverage separately.
Use dimension-aware sample budgets without changing the fixed total budget.
risks: A large nominal point count can still leave high-dimensional projections poorly covered.

macro_physics_principles.title: Darcy flux and heterogeneous conductivity balance
macro_physics_principles.implication: Darcy flow is governed by the divergence of a coefficient-weighted gradient, so pressure accuracy and physical flux accuracy are inseparable.
design_requirements: Resolve gradients where conductivity changes rapidly.
Audit coefficient-weighted flux as well as pressure error.
Preserve the registered conductivity field exactly.
risks: A smooth pressure approximation can hide a large local flux error in a high-contrast medium.

macro_physics_principles.title: Nonlinear elliptic screening balance
macro_physics_principles.implication: The elliptic curvature term and nonlinear screening term must balance over the full geometry, including regions where the potential makes the nonlinear response steep.
design_requirements: Monitor the differential and nonlinear residual contributions separately.
Resolve nonlinear hotspots and every boundary component.
risks: Loss domination by either curvature or screening can produce a low aggregate residual with incorrect potential amplitude.

macro_physics_principles.title: Shallow-water conservative hyperbolic coupling
macro_physics_principles.implication: Water depth and both momentum components form one conservative hyperbolic state whose characteristic speeds and fluxes depend on the state itself.
design_requirements: Retain mass and both momentum residuals.
Monitor component-wise and global conservation error.
Keep the conservative state coupling intact.
risks: Optimizing one momentum component or pointwise fit alone can violate mass conservation or wave propagation.

macro_physics_principles.title: Positive water-depth admissibility
macro_physics_principles.implication: Non-positive water depth is outside the physical state space and also makes velocity and wave-speed interpretations singular or invalid.
design_requirements: Track minimum predicted depth and positivity violations explicitly.
Balance bound enforcement with conservation residuals.
risks: A small MSE can coexist with localized negative depth.

macro_physics_principles.title: Kuramoto-Sivashinsky fourth-order chaotic balance
macro_physics_principles.implication: Destabilizing low-order dynamics, fourth-order dissipation, nonlinearity, and periodic topology jointly determine the active modes and chaotic trajectory.
design_requirements: Preserve all derivative orders and their coefficients.
Audit periodic value and derivative consistency.
Evaluate early-time trajectory fidelity and active-mode content.
risks: Suppressing high derivatives may stabilize training while solving the wrong dynamics.

macro_physics_principles.title: Multiscale and anisotropic heat diffusion
macro_physics_principles.implication: Diffusion damps different spatial modes at different rates, while anisotropy makes resolution requirements direction dependent.
design_requirements: Resolve the fastest initial modes before they decay.
Audit errors by spatial direction and scale.
risks: Late-time accuracy can conceal failure to reproduce high-frequency early transients.

macro_physics_principles.title: Long-time dissipative evolution
macro_physics_principles.implication: Long-time heat evolution is a cumulative dissipative process whose early transient and decay rates determine the later state.
design_requirements: Resolve early transients and late low-amplitude states.
Avoid weighting schemes that ignore either end of the time interval.
risks: Uniform absolute loss can underweight late states after the solution amplitude decays.

macro_physics_principles.title: Heterogeneous wave speed, refraction, and local wavelength
macro_physics_principles.implication: A varying wave speed changes local wavelength, travel time, and propagation direction, concentrating phase error near strong coefficient gradients.
design_requirements: Monitor local phase and travel-time error.
Maintain boundary conditions while refining heterogeneous regions.
risks: A single global frequency scale can underresolve slow-wave regions or overcondition fast-wave regions.

macro_physics_principles.title: Inverse data information and regularization balance
macro_physics_principles.implication: Noisy observations provide uneven information about latent fields or parameters, while the PDE supplies structured but potentially biased regularization.
design_requirements: Separate data fit, state error, parameter error, and PDE violation.
risks: Overweighting data overfits noise; overweighting physics can erase identifiable observation information.

macro_physics_principles.title: Pressure gauge and uniqueness
macro_physics_principles.implication: In incompressible flow, pressure is defined only up to an additive constant unless the registered gauge or equivalent condition is enforced.
design_requirements: Report gauge error separately from pressure gradients.
Do not let dense velocity constraints overwhelm the gauge.
risks: Correct velocity and pressure gradients can coexist with an arbitrary pressure offset.

macro_physics_principles.title: Reaction-diffusion interface and pattern dynamics
macro_physics_principles.implication: Reaction-diffusion solutions often concentrate informative error at moving interfaces, fronts, or emerging pattern boundaries rather than uniformly in space-time.
design_requirements: Track interface or pattern-region error when present.
Retain global samples while resolving moving localized structure.
risks: Uniform average error can hide misplaced fronts or incorrect pattern wavelength.

macro_physics_principles.title: Derivative-order fidelity
macro_physics_principles.implication: Every derivative order registered by the governing equation contributes to the physical balance and must be represented accurately, not merely evaluated symbolically.
design_requirements: Use a representation differentiable to the required order.
Do not suppress a difficult derivative term without physical justification.
risks: A smooth-looking state can have inaccurate derivatives and therefore violate the PDE strongly.

macro_physics_principles.title: Competing high-order derivative scales
macro_physics_principles.implication: High-order PDEs can combine derivative terms with sharply different magnitudes and spectral effects, so term-wise fidelity matters more than aggregate cancellation.
design_requirements: Distinguish physical cancellation from numerical cancellation.
risks: Large inaccurate terms may cancel in the aggregate residual while the learned dynamics remain wrong.

macro_physics_principles.title: Periodic value, derivative, and flux topology
macro_physics_principles.implication: Identified periodic faces must agree in all state and derivative or flux quantities required by the PDE order and conservation form.
design_requirements: Audit state and relevant derivative continuity.
Check global flux closure across the seam.
risks: Matching values alone can leave derivative jumps that act as artificial sources.

macro_physics_principles.title: Neumann and Robin flux compatibility
macro_physics_principles.implication: Derivative-valued boundary conditions constrain normal flux and may also participate in global compatibility or uniqueness conditions.
design_requirements: Evaluate normal derivatives with the registered orientation.
Audit boundary flux separately from interior residual.
risks: Sign, normal-direction, or scaling errors can corrupt the global solution despite low interior residual.

macro_physics_principles.title: Two-dimensional Burgers vector-flux coupling
macro_physics_principles.implication: Both velocity components participate in multidirectional nonlinear transport and share the same evolving shock and periodic topology.
design_requirements: Monitor both residual components and cross-advection terms.
Preserve paired periodic constraints in both axes.
risks: One component can dominate the aggregate loss and mask incorrect transverse transport.

macro_physics_principles.title: Allen-Cahn phase bounds and dissipative energy
macro_physics_principles.implication: Allen-Cahn evolution moves diffuse interfaces while relaxing a double-well free energy and keeping the phase field near its physically relevant states.
design_requirements: Resolve moving interface width and location.
Track phase overshoot and energy trend when available.
risks: Excess smoothing can reduce residual while broadening the interface and changing its velocity.

macro_physics_principles.title: Gray-Scott species balance and pattern-scale selection
macro_physics_principles.implication: Coupled feed, kill, reaction, and unequal diffusion rates select evolving spatial pattern scales and species amplitudes over a long horizon.
design_requirements: Track pattern wavelength and contrast as well as pointwise error.
Preserve early nucleation and later pattern evolution.
risks: A blurred or phase-shifted pattern may have modest average error but incorrect dynamics.

macro_physics_principles.title: Variable-coefficient transient heat flux
macro_physics_principles.implication: Space-time variation in the diffusion coefficient changes both local smoothing rates and the coefficient-weighted flux throughout evolution.
design_requirements: Sample coefficient extremes over space and time.
Audit local flux and time derivative balance.
risks: Sampling only high solution amplitude can miss difficult coefficient regimes.

macro_physics_principles.title: Complex-geometry heat flow with mixed flux boundaries
macro_physics_principles.implication: Multiple hole boundaries and Robin conditions jointly control heat exchange, making local normal orientation and component coverage physically significant.
design_requirements: Cover every hole boundary over time.
Audit value and normal-flux parts of Robin conditions.
risks: Under-sampling one hole or using an incorrect normal changes the global heat balance.

macro_physics_principles.title: Five-dimensional heat geometry and radial boundary measure
macro_physics_principles.implication: High-dimensional radial geometry concentrates sampling measure differently from a box, while the Neumann boundary constrains a normal derivative on the hypersurface.
design_requirements: Separate radial boundary and interior coverage.
Audit derivative accuracy along boundary normals.
risks: Box-style sampling intuition can misrepresent both volume and surface distributions.

macro_physics_principles.title: Long-time wave energy and phase drift
macro_physics_principles.implication: Small frequency bias accumulates into large phase drift over 50 temporal cycles, while the hyperbolic spatial modes make the reference amplitude reach O(sinh(3*pi)).
design_requirements: Audit time-slice phase and amplitude proxies.
Preserve the registered initial displacement, zero initial velocity, and spatial Dirichlet constraints.
Maintain coverage across the full horizon.
Account explicitly for the large physical output scale.
When using a separable temporal ansatz, derive it only from registered initial-state and frequency information.
risks: Low short-time error does not establish long-time fidelity.
Omitting the initial velocity leaves a second-order-in-time problem underdetermined.
An unscaled network can minimize the homogeneous PDE residual by collapsing toward the zero solution.

macro_physics_principles.title: Lid-driven cavity wall, corner, and vortex dynamics
macro_physics_principles.implication: The moving lid, stationary walls, corner singular behavior, and recirculating vortex couple boundary accuracy to the entire pressure-velocity field.
design_requirements: Track divergence and wall slip separately.
risks: Uniform boundary error can hide localized corner and moving-wall defects that shift the vortex.

macro_physics_principles.title: Backward-step separation and recirculation
macro_physics_principles.implication: The step generates localized separation, recirculation, and reattachment whose location depends on wall geometry, pressure gradient, and incompressibility.
design_requirements: Resolve the step corner and downstream shear layer.
Audit reverse flow and reattachment region.
Maintain all wall and inlet/outlet conditions.
risks: Global velocity MSE can remain modest with an incorrect recirculation length.

macro_physics_principles.title: Long-time incompressible vorticity transport
macro_physics_principles.implication: Long-time velocity evolution transports and diffuses vorticity while pressure enforces incompressibility, allowing early local errors to contaminate later flow structure.
design_requirements: Track divergence and time-slice momentum errors.
risks: A plausible late velocity field can conceal accumulated divergence or vorticity error.

macro_physics_principles.title: Many-subdomain elliptic transmission network
macro_physics_principles.implication: A grid of coefficient subdomains forms a connected transmission network in which local state and flux mismatches propagate through the global elliptic solution.
design_requirements: Cover every subdomain and interface class.
Preserve the external Robin boundary separately.
risks: Average interface error can hide one poorly resolved subdomain junction.

macro_physics_principles.title: Neumann Poisson compatibility and nullspace control
macro_physics_principles.implication: Neumann elliptic problems require compatible net flux and may retain an additive constant unless the registered contract supplies a normalization.
design_requirements: Separate gradient accuracy from constant-offset error.
risks: A nearly correct gradient field may have a large arbitrary offset or incompatible net flux.

macro_physics_principles.title: Five-dimensional global elliptic coupling
macro_physics_principles.implication: The five-dimensional elliptic solution couples forcing and the full hypercube boundary globally, while sparse projections may conceal coverage gaps.
design_requirements: Audit global and low-dimensional projection errors.
Cover corners, faces, and interior without tensor-grid explosion.
Maintain second derivatives in every coordinate.
risks: Good accuracy on selected slices does not imply coverage of the high-dimensional domain.

macro_physics_principles.title: Inverse Poisson source-state non-uniqueness control
macro_physics_principles.implication: Sparse noisy observations may permit compensating errors between the state and inferred source or coefficient unless boundary and PDE information constrain both.
design_requirements: Report state and inferred quantity separately.
Audit sensitivity to observation placement and noise.
risks: Accurate observed values can coexist with an incorrect inferred physical field away from sensors.

macro_physics_principles.title: Inverse heat temporal identifiability
macro_physics_principles.implication: Diffusion progressively erases high-frequency information, so observation time placement strongly affects which latent quantities remain identifiable.
design_requirements: Distinguish early and late observation information.
Audit inferred quantities beyond sensor times.
Balance transient PDE and data evidence.
risks: Late observations alone may not identify fine-scale initial or coefficient structure.

macro_physics_principles.title: Periodic shallow-water global mass closure
macro_physics_principles.implication: With periodic boundaries and no registered source, total water mass must remain closed while local mass and momentum waves circulate through the domain.
design_requirements: Evaluate local conservation together with depth positivity.
risks: Small local residual bias can accumulate into global mass drift.

macro_physics_principles.title: Kovasznay pressure-velocity mode consistency
macro_physics_principles.implication: The analytic Kovasznay field couples exponential velocity decay, transverse oscillation, pressure variation, incompressibility, and a pressure gauge.
design_requirements: Resolve both exponential and oscillatory spatial modes.
risks: Velocity can appear accurate while pressure amplitude or gauge remains wrong.

macro_physics_principles.title: Poisson-Boltzmann geometry-nonlinearity interaction
macro_physics_principles.implication: Nonlinear screening strength and the four-hole boundary topology interact to localize curvature and potential gradients near selected boundary regions.
design_requirements: Track nonlinear-response and curvature errors near boundaries.
risks: Treating all boundary components as statistically identical can miss geometry-dependent nonlinear hotspots.

macro_physics_principles.title: Darcy coercivity and energy-norm fidelity
macro_physics_principles.implication: Positive heterogeneous conductivity weights gradient error non-uniformly, making coefficient-weighted energy or flux fidelity more informative than state MSE alone.
design_requirements: Track coefficient-weighted residual or flux diagnostics.
risks: Low pressure MSE can coexist with poor energy-norm accuracy.

macro_physics_principles.title: Local residual and global solution consistency
macro_physics_principles.implication: Pointwise residual samples, global field metrics, constraint errors, and physically meaningful derived quantities measure different aspects of the same solution and must agree before a candidate is trusted.
design_requirements: Compare residual, state, and constraint diagnostics.
Do not infer physical accuracy from one aggregate metric.
risks: A candidate can exploit sparse evaluation coverage or cancellation in an aggregate score.

macro_physics_principles.title: One-dimensional viscous-shock thickness and location
macro_physics_principles.implication: The registered viscosity sets a narrow but finite shock thickness while nonlinear transport determines its location and time evolution.
design_requirements: Distinguish physical viscous smoothing from neural spectral bias.
risks: A broad displaced transition can have moderate MSE but incorrect transport and dissipation.

macro_physics_principles.title: Long-time heat modal decay hierarchy
macro_physics_principles.implication: Fast spatial modes vanish early while slow modes dominate the long tail, producing a large dynamic range across time slices.
design_requirements: Resolve early fast modes and late slow modes.
Audit relative as well as absolute time-slice error.
risks: Aggregate absolute loss can ignore the low-amplitude long-time tail.

macro_physics_principles.title: Multiscale heat early-mode decay
macro_physics_principles.implication: The highest-frequency anisotropic modes contain important initial information but decay on the shortest physical time scales.
design_requirements: Concentrate diagnostic resolution near the initial time without dropping late samples.
Preserve low-frequency modes after fast-mode decay.
risks: A model trained mainly at later times can miss the defining multiscale transient.

macro_physics_principles.title: Classic Poisson hole-boundary global coupling
macro_physics_principles.implication: The outer and internal hole boundaries jointly determine the globally coupled elliptic field, including gradients concentrated near curved boundaries.
design_requirements: Cover outer and inner boundaries separately.
risks: A small internal boundary can influence the whole field while contributing few uniformly sampled points.

macro_physics_principles.title: One-dimensional wave standing-mode initial state
macro_physics_principles.implication: The registered displacement and velocity initialize the modal amplitude and phase, which boundary conditions then propagate through the full space-time domain.
design_requirements: Resolve the registered spatial and temporal frequencies.
Audit amplitude and phase over time.
risks: A small initial-velocity defect produces systematic phase drift.

macro_physics_principles.title: Hyperbolic characteristic propagation
macro_physics_principles.implication: Information propagates along characteristic families at finite speeds, making front location, boundary inflow direction, and causal domain of dependence central to fidelity.
design_requirements: Audit propagation speed and front location.
risks: A globally small residual can hide phase or characteristic-speed error.

macro_physics_principles.title: Compressible-flow entropy admissibility
macro_physics_principles.implication: Conservation laws with shocks admit multiple weak solutions, and the physically realized branch satisfies an entropy admissibility condition.
design_requirements: Monitor entropy production or admissibility diagnostics.
risks: Pointwise residual minimization may converge to a nonphysical weak solution.

macro_physics_principles.title: Positive density, pressure, and internal energy
macro_physics_principles.implication: Density, pressure, and internal energy must remain in the thermodynamically admissible state set.
risks: Localized negative states can invalidate fluxes even when average error is small.

macro_physics_principles.title: Contact and material discontinuity transport
macro_physics_principles.implication: Contact waves transport jumps in state or material properties without the same entropy production as shocks.
design_requirements: Preserve interface speed and jump conditions.
risks: Shock-focused refinement can smear or misclassify contact waves.

macro_physics_principles.title: Singular perturbation and boundary layers
macro_physics_principles.implication: A small physical parameter can create thin boundary or internal layers whose width vanishes asymptotically while the outer solution remains smooth.
risks: Uniform approximation may fit the outer solution and entirely miss the layer.

macro_physics_principles.title: Anisotropic tensor diffusion
macro_physics_principles.implication: A diffusion tensor selects direction-dependent smoothing and flux scales through its eigenstructure.
design_requirements: Preserve positive definiteness and coefficient orientation.
risks: Isotropic resolution can underfit the stiff direction and waste samples elsewhere.

macro_physics_principles.title: Degenerate nonlinear diffusion
macro_physics_principles.implication: State-dependent diffusivity may vanish or become singular, changing regularity and allowing compact support or moving fronts.
design_requirements: Resolve degeneracy regions and moving support.
Audit nonlinear flux rather than only the state.
risks: Assuming uniformly parabolic smoothing can destroy finite-speed behavior.

macro_physics_principles.title: Porous-medium finite-speed support propagation
macro_physics_principles.implication: Porous-medium diffusion can preserve compact support and move its boundary at finite speed while conserving mass under closed conditions.
design_requirements: Track support boundary and total mass.
Resolve both active and zero-state regions.
risks: Smooth neural tails can create nonphysical instantaneous propagation.

macro_physics_principles.title: Elliptic coercivity and nullspace structure
macro_physics_principles.implication: Elliptic stability depends on coercivity modulo any physical nullspace such as constants or rigid motions.
design_requirements: Identify and constrain registered null modes.
Preserve all conditions required for uniqueness.
risks: Residual minimization can drift along an unconstrained nullspace.

macro_physics_principles.title: Mixed boundary partition consistency
macro_physics_principles.implication: Different boundary subsets may prescribe values, fluxes, impedances, or periodic identifications and must remain disjoint, complete, and orientation consistent.
risks: Aggregate boundary loss can conceal a missing or contradictory subset.

macro_physics_principles.title: Singular source and reduced regularity
macro_physics_principles.implication: Point sources, re-entrant corners, or singular coefficients reduce solution regularity and invalidate globally smooth error assumptions.
design_requirements: Evaluate away from and near singularities separately.
risks: Global smoothing can erase the correct singular asymptotics.

macro_physics_principles.title: Elastic stress-strain-equilibrium compatibility
macro_physics_principles.implication: Displacement, strain, stress, constitutive response, and force balance form one compatible mechanical system.
design_requirements: Respect stress symmetry and boundary tractions.
risks: Accurate displacement values can coexist with poor stress derivatives.

macro_physics_principles.title: Elastic rigid-body nullspace
macro_physics_principles.implication: Pure or insufficient traction conditions leave rigid translations or rotations unconstrained even when strain energy is correct.
design_requirements: Separate strain accuracy from absolute displacement.
risks: Low equilibrium residual does not establish a unique displacement field.

macro_physics_principles.title: Nearly incompressible material limit
macro_physics_principles.implication: Large bulk-to-shear modulus ratios create a stiff volumetric constraint analogous to incompressibility.
design_requirements: Use mixed variables only when registered.
risks: Penalty domination can lock deformation or destroy stress accuracy.

macro_physics_principles.title: Maxwell curl-divergence compatibility
macro_physics_principles.implication: Electric and magnetic curl evolution must remain compatible with Gauss divergence constraints and charge conservation.
design_requirements: Audit field components and constraints separately.
risks: Accurate curl dynamics can accumulate nonphysical divergence modes.

macro_physics_principles.title: Electromagnetic material-interface transmission
macro_physics_principles.implication: Tangential fields and material-weighted normal fluxes obey distinct jump conditions across electromagnetic interfaces.
design_requirements: Resolve both sides of each interface.
Audit tangential and normal transmission separately.
risks: Naive continuity can impose the wrong physics at coefficient jumps.

macro_physics_principles.title: Wave energy and boundary flux balance
macro_physics_principles.implication: Wave energy changes only through registered sources, damping, or boundary flux, linking amplitude evolution to boundary treatment.
design_requirements: Distinguish physical damping from numerical damping.
risks: Phase-correct waves may still exhibit nonphysical amplitude growth or decay.

macro_physics_principles.title: Helmholtz resonance and high-wavenumber pollution
macro_physics_principles.implication: High wavenumber and near-resonant regimes amplify phase error and may make stability depend strongly on boundary impedance and domain geometry.
risks: Low average residual can coexist with systematic wavelength pollution.

macro_physics_principles.title: Eigenfunction normalization and orthogonality
macro_physics_principles.implication: PDE eigenproblems require a nontrivial normalization and, for multiple modes, orthogonality or ordering constraints.
design_requirements: Enforce orthogonality and audit eigenvalue residual.
risks: Residual minimization alone admits the trivial zero solution.

macro_physics_principles.title: Fourth-order elliptic boundary completeness
macro_physics_principles.implication: Fourth-order elliptic problems need two compatible boundary conditions and accurate curvature or moment quantities.
design_requirements: Audit deflection and derivative boundary data.
risks: Value-only boundary enforcement leaves the plate problem under-constrained.

macro_physics_principles.title: Phase-field free-energy dissipation
macro_physics_principles.implication: Phase-field dynamics evolve diffuse interfaces according to a free-energy landscape and a problem-specific conserved or nonconserved gradient flow.
design_requirements: Track interface width and free energy.
risks: Smoothing the field may lower residual while changing interfacial energy.

macro_physics_principles.title: Cahn-Hilliard mass conservation and fourth-order flow
macro_physics_principles.implication: Cahn-Hilliard evolution conserves total order parameter while dissipating energy through a fourth-order or mixed chemical-potential system.
risks: Accurate local patterns can coexist with slow global mass drift.

macro_physics_principles.title: Dispersive phase and group velocity
macro_physics_principles.implication: Different Fourier modes propagate at different phase and group velocities, so spectral balance determines wave-packet shape and location.
risks: Amplitude fit can hide incorrect packet speed or spectral spreading.

macro_physics_principles.title: Schrodinger norm and complex-phase invariance
macro_physics_principles.implication: Real and imaginary components form one complex field with global phase symmetry and conserved or controlled norm under closed evolution.
risks: Component-wise MSE can misrepresent a harmless global phase or hide norm drift.

macro_physics_principles.title: KdV soliton balance and invariants
macro_physics_principles.implication: KdV solitons arise from nonlinear steepening balanced by third-order dispersion and satisfy integral invariants.
design_requirements: Resolve soliton amplitude, width, and speed.
risks: Artificial diffusion broadens solitons and changes collision behavior.

macro_physics_principles.title: Hamilton-Jacobi viscosity-solution admissibility
macro_physics_principles.implication: Hamilton-Jacobi equations develop gradient discontinuities and select a unique viscosity solution through a comparison principle.
design_requirements: Audit gradient and value errors separately.
risks: Classical residuals are unreliable exactly where the viscosity solution is nonsmooth.

macro_physics_principles.title: Eikonal gradient norm, fronts, and caustics
macro_physics_principles.implication: The eikonal field encodes travel time or distance through a gradient-norm constraint and can be nonsmooth at caustics or medial axes.
design_requirements: Anchor source or boundary travel time.
Treat caustics as physical nonsmooth sets.
risks: A smooth approximation can round caustics and bias travel time globally.

macro_physics_principles.title: Free-boundary kinematic and dynamic coupling
macro_physics_principles.implication: The unknown interface location and the field solution determine one another through kinematic motion and dynamic or flux jump conditions.
design_requirements: Track topology and motion over time.
risks: A small field residual on the wrong moving domain is not a valid solution.

macro_physics_principles.title: Moving-domain geometric conservation
macro_physics_principles.implication: Coordinate motion changes volume and flux measures and must satisfy a geometric conservation identity.
design_requirements: Preserve mesh or coordinate velocity terms.
risks: Ignoring geometric terms introduces artificial sources in an otherwise conservative PDE.

macro_physics_principles.title: Fractional and nonlocal tail coupling
macro_physics_principles.implication: Fractional operators couple each point to a broad spatial or temporal neighborhood and require exterior or history data beyond local boundaries.
risks: Local collocation alone cannot represent a genuinely nonlocal operator.

macro_physics_principles.title: Integral-operator domain balance
macro_physics_principles.implication: Kernel integrals mix local states with global or directional information and introduce quadrature error distinct from neural approximation error.
risks: Sparse or biased quadrature can make an incorrect network appear PDE-consistent.

macro_physics_principles.title: Stochastic-PDE distributional consistency
macro_physics_principles.implication: A stochastic PDE defines a family of physical solutions over random inputs, so moments, tails, and pathwise constraints all matter.
design_requirements: Audit moments and tail events separately.
risks: Mean accuracy can conceal incorrect variance or rare-event behavior.

macro_physics_principles.title: Uniform validity over a parametric PDE family
macro_physics_principles.implication: A parametric solver must satisfy the PDE across the full parameter domain rather than interpolate a few easy parameter instances.
risks: Random average sampling can ignore a small hard parameter regime.

macro_physics_principles.title: Multiphysics interface exchange balance
macro_physics_principles.implication: Coupled subsystems exchange conserved quantities or work through interfaces, requiring equal-and-opposite or constitutively linked transfer.
design_requirements: Audit interface exchange from both sides.
risks: Each subsystem can look accurate while their interface transfer is inconsistent.

macro_physics_principles.title: Magnetohydrodynamic divergence and energy coupling
macro_physics_principles.implication: Fluid and magnetic fields exchange momentum and energy while the magnetic field remains divergence-free.
risks: Small momentum residual can coexist with nonphysical magnetic monopoles.

macro_physics_principles.title: Thermoelastic bidirectional coupling
macro_physics_principles.implication: Temperature changes induce strain and mechanical work may feed back into thermal evolution, coupling fields with different units and time scales.
design_requirements: Audit energy exchange and boundary conditions.
risks: One-way fitting can silently discard registered feedback.

macro_physics_principles.title: Fluid-structure traction and velocity continuity
macro_physics_principles.implication: Fluid and solid share interface velocity or displacement and exchange equal-and-opposite traction on a moving boundary.
risks: Small subsystem residuals do not guarantee interface equilibrium.

macro_physics_principles.title: Physical symmetry and invariance reduction
macro_physics_principles.implication: Known symmetries map valid solutions to valid solutions and can reduce effective complexity without changing the physical contract.
risks: Incorrect symmetry assumptions exclude legitimate solutions.

macro_physics_principles.title: Dimensionless characteristic regimes
macro_physics_principles.implication: Dimensionless groups identify dominant physical balances and transition regimes more reliably than raw coefficient magnitude alone.
design_requirements: Relate design choices to the active dimensionless regime.
risks: Arbitrary normalization can obscure the dominant balance or alter parameter meaning.

macro_physics_principles.title: PDE invariance on manifolds and curved surfaces
macro_physics_principles.implication: Surface gradients, divergence, and Laplace-Beltrami operators depend on geometry but physical results must be coordinate invariant.
design_requirements: Respect the manifold metric and measure.
risks: Applying Euclidean derivatives to embedded coordinates solves the wrong PDE.

macro_physics_principles.title: Local-to-global integral conservation closure
macro_physics_principles.implication: Integrating a local conservation law links total content change to boundary flux and registered sources.
risks: Small biased local residuals can accumulate into large global drift.

macro_physics_principles.title: Source, sink, and boundary budget balance
macro_physics_principles.implication: Registered forcing, reaction, dissipation, and boundary exchange determine the net budget of physical quantities.
design_requirements: Keep source and sink signs and units.
Distinguish internal exchange from net creation.
risks: Aggregate cancellation can hide individually incorrect source and sink terms.

macro_physics_principles.title: Inverse uncertainty and non-uniqueness
macro_physics_principles.implication: Finite noisy data may support multiple parameter or field explanations consistent with the PDE.
design_requirements: Report parameter and state uncertainty when available.
Test sensitivity to data and initialization.
Avoid claiming uniqueness from one optimum.
risks: A precise optimizer result can be physically non-identifiable.

macro_physics_principles.title: Causal observation influence in data assimilation
macro_physics_principles.implication: Observations constrain state trajectories according to temporal causality and model dynamics rather than as independent point labels.
design_requirements: Audit interpolation and forecast intervals separately.
risks: Overfitting sensors can create dynamically inconsistent paths between observations.

macro_physics_principles.title: Distributional and weak-solution balance
macro_physics_principles.implication: When classical derivatives do not exist, physical validity is expressed through integrated weak balance and jump conditions.
design_requirements: Use supported weak or conservative diagnostics.
Do not demand artificial classical smoothness.
risks: Strong residuals near discontinuities can be undefined or misleading.

macro_physics_principles.title: Maximum-principle and comparison bounds
macro_physics_principles.implication: Many elliptic and parabolic equations constrain interior extrema through boundary, initial, forcing, and reaction data.
design_requirements: Relate extrema to the registered comparison principle.
Separate physical overshoot from approximation noise.
risks: Small MSE can coexist with localized violation of a qualitative bound.

macro_physics_principles.title: Monotonicity and order preservation
macro_physics_principles.implication: Some PDE semigroups preserve ordering or monotonic structure inherited from data and forcing.
design_requirements: Audit known monotone directions or comparisons.
risks: Generic monotonic constraints can wrongly exclude oscillatory physical solutions.

macro_physics_principles.title: Continuous dependence and stability regime
macro_physics_principles.implication: A well-posed PDE maps perturbations in data and parameters to solution changes according to a problem-dependent stability constant or growth law.
design_requirements: Interpret error in the correct stability regime.
Track amplification over space or time.
risks: Identical residual tolerances imply very different state errors across PDE regimes.

macro_physics_principles.title: Differential-algebraic constraint-manifold invariance
macro_physics_principles.implication: Differential evolution must remain on the algebraic constraint manifold, and inconsistent initial data or drift can invalidate the trajectory.
design_requirements: Enforce algebraic constraints and consistent initialization.
Respect constraint index and derivative coupling.
risks: Small differential residual can coexist with growing algebraic inconsistency.

macro_physics_principles.title: Boundary-flux orientation and conservation
macro_physics_principles.implication: Conservative boundary exchange depends on outward-normal orientation and on whether characteristics or fluxes enter or leave the domain.
risks: A normal-sign error reverses sources and sinks at the boundary.
